name: Hotel Helvetia & Bristol
positioning: Helvetia & Bristol Firenze, a Starhotels Collezione hotel welcoming guests since 1885, between Via Tornabuoni and Piazza della Repubblica, with Cibrèo dining and an underground spa in former bank vaults
best_for: Travelers who want a walkable base between Via Tornabuoni and Piazza della Repubblica, across from Palazzo Strozzi
Spa lovers who want a Roman-style thermal circuit without leaving the hotel
Food-focused guests drawn to Cibrèo and Iginio Massari pastries at breakfast

facts.text: Helvetia & Bristol has welcomed guests since 1885, when Florence was a popular stop on the Grand Tour.
The hotel lies between the shopping street Via Tornabuoni and Piazza della Repubblica.
Palazzo Strozzi, which hosts a rolling program of exhibitions, is across the road.
Rooms in the Helvetia Wing are furnished with antique furniture and meticulously restored works of art.
The contemporary suites in the Bristol wing were designed by Anouska Hempel.
In 2021 the hotel expanded into the 19th-century building next door, once the headquarters of the Banca di Roma.
The hotel's restaurant and bar are run by Cibrèo, a Florentine institution.
Cibrèo Ristorante & Cocktail Bar serves a seasonal menu in spaces designed by Italian architect Massimo Adario.
The spa's thermal circuit includes a calidarium, tepidarium, sudatorium and frigidarium, plus spa pools.
LA SPA is underground, housed in the building's old bank vaults.
The Panoramic Suite Helvetia, on the fifth floor, has city views that include the Duomo and Giotto's Campanile.
The concierge can arrange private city tours, vineyard visits and personal shopper sessions.

highlights.text: LA SPA is the largest spa in Florence's historic center.
The spa's tepidarium has a glass floor through which you can see the building's medieval foundations.
The breakfast spread, set up in the Tinello, includes pastries, cakes, cookies and croissants baked daily at Galleria Iginio Massari in Florence.
The Winter Garden is crowned by a historic Liberty-style glass ceiling.
Guests get access to the Circolo del Tennis Firenze 1898, including its clay tennis and padel courts.

considerations.text: The spa is open to non-residents, so hotel guests share it with locals.
The style depends on the wing: Helvetia Wing rooms have antiques and restored artworks, while the Bristol wing suites are contemporary.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.
